entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Xin Qiji was a Chinese poet, calligrapher, and military general during the Southern Song dynasty (1127–1279).

As a key figure associated with the Southern Song court, Xin Qiji played a crucial role in the artistic and cultural landscape of the time. His poetry and calligraphy are still studied and admired today for their beauty and technical skill.

Xin Qiji's military campaigns took him to the southern regions of China, where he fought against the Jin dynasty. His experiences during this period had a lasting impact on his poetry and worldview.

Despite his military background, Xin Qiji was also a patron of the arts, supporting many artists and writers during his lifetime. His legacy can be seen in the many artists and writers who followed in his footsteps.

In his later years, Xin Qiji became increasingly reclusive, preferring the company of his own thoughts to the world outside. He died in 1207, leaving behind a body of work that continues to inspire and delight readers to this day.
